subject: Clarify Billing Anchor Scope in Pricing Exhibit — Legal Footnotes
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@solacehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@solacehealth.com, james.lee@solacehealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on Exhibit B billing anchor and floor application

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the updated Exhibit B (attached). Our procurement team ran a quick pass and surfaced an ambiguity in the pricing anchor language. Specifically: when a single invoice includes a mix of metered "per-token" SKUs and a non-metered fixed-seat SKU that are bundled in the same "package", is the anchor/floor applied per SKU, per package, or at the aggregate account level?

Examples we care about:
- If package A contains 2 metered SKUs + 1 seat-based SKU, and package B is purely metered, do anchors apply separately to each package, or is the invoice aggregated across both packages before evaluating the floor?

This matters for how our spend true-ups will calculate and for our auditors. We prefer the anchor to be applied at the package level, but legal flagged that the current footnote is silent. Could your team propose explicit footnote language (or confirm the intended interpretation)?

Attaching Exhibit B v3 for reference.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Procurement Lead
Solace Health

Attachments: Solace_ExhibitB_v3.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@solacehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.coole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on Exhibit B billing anchor and floor application

Hi Ellen —

Appreciate the clear example — good catch. Intent was to anchor at the billing family / package level, not to force cross-package aggregation that could create over-crediting for mixed bundles. That said, the current draft does leave room for different interpretations, so we should add a clarifying footnote. Two practical options:

1) Explicit footnote: "Anchors and floors apply at the billing family (package) level; where a package contains both metered and non-metered SKUs, the invoice-level true-up shall allocate spend to the package in accordance with the operational definition of 'billable unit family' in the pricing appendix."

2) Commercial compromise: accept Solace's request for package-level anchors but include a 90-day post-go-live true-up window for the first six months to catch any classification errors.

I've attached a quick markup with option 1 language highlighted (Contract_Markup_jonas.pdf). Marissa — can legal weigh in on the footnote text below? Laura / Karthik — would option 2 be acceptable commercially if legal prefers a simpler anchor language?

Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Director
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Contract_Markup_jonas.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700

On Mon, May 10, 2027 at 12:45 PM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Appreciate the clear example — good catch. Intent was to anchor at the billing family / package level...

Ellen / team — looping in legal. We reviewed Jonas's proposed footnote and have two drafting recommendations to prevent downstream disputes and limit revenue leakage:

1) Define "billable unit family" operationally in the pricing appendix (examples + mapping table).
2) Add a parenthetical that for mixed packages, the allocation hierarchy is: (a) package-level allocation by explicit SKU mapping, (b) if mapping is absent, allocate proportionally by invoiced list price, and (c) disputed allocations are subject to the 45-day true-up notice in Section 6.2.

Proposed footnote text (suggested insertion to Exhibit B):
"For purposes of this Exhibit, 'billable unit family' means the grouping of SKUs as set forth in the pricing appendix. Anchors and floors shall apply to each billable unit family. Where a billable unit family includes both metered and non-metered SKUs, spend shall be allocated to the family in accordance with the mapping table; absent an explicit mapping, allocation shall be performed pro rata by list price. Any allocation dispute shall be resolved in accordance with the contract's true-up and dispute mechanisms"

Operational ask: can Jonas or Laura produce the SKU -> billing family mapping (a short spreadsheet) for Solace before we finalize? I placed the draft footnote in a tracked doc here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcXYZ-exhibitb-ops-def and attached an editable Word version (ExhibitB_Legal_Footnote_Draft.docx).

Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachments: ExhibitB_Legal_Footnote_Draft.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: ellen.park@solacehealth.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on Exhibit B billing anchor and floor application

Thanks — quick commercial note from my side.

I support the operational definition but want a pragmatic commercial guardrail to keep Solace comfortable and protect Redwood economics while we ramp:

- Anchor application: billable family (per Marissa's draft).
- For the first six billing cycles post go-live, apply a quarterly "reconciliation collar": if allocation variances cause invoice movement > +/- 4% vs projected bill, the parties will true-up but credits are capped to 7.5% of that quarter's billed amount.
- After six cycles, collar removed and allocations follow the mapping table.

Rationale: reduces audit churn for both sides while giving Solace the package-level certainty they want. If legal insists on immediate uncapped true-ups, we should push for a shortened notice window (45 days) rather than leave the floor ambiguous.

Ellen — can you confirm whether Solace would accept the 7.5% cap for the initial ramp (or suggest an alternative cap)? If yes, Marissa can fold into the footnote + SOW.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@solacehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on Exhibit B billing anchor and floor application

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. Solace accepts the billable family definition and the proposed reconciliation collar, with two small adjustments:

1) True-up cadence: prefer quarterly true-ups (end of quarter), not a rolling 90-day period — operationally easier for our finance team.
2) Cap tweak: we can accept the 7.5% cap, but would like the cap to apply per-quarter on a net basis (credits net against invoiced charges) rather than per-invoice.

If you can fold these two points into the footnote and add the SKU->family mapping to the pricing appendix (spreadsheet) we'll route redlines here and get to DocuSign next week.

Ellen Park
Procurement Lead
Solace Health
